title: Four datasets, one set of numbers
hook: Four datasets with the same mean, spread and correlation. Do they share one best-fit line?

doesNotKnow: that summary numbers can hide the shape of the data

misconception: Two datasets with the same mean, spread and correlation look alike.
objective: The learner can explain that the same means, spread, correlation and best-fit line can come from very different pictures (a cloud, a curve, an outlier, one extreme point), so the data should always be drawn.
keyState: The fitted line y = 3.00 + 0.50x shown on all four plots, with r = 0.82 each time.

claims.text: The four datasets are Anscombe's quartet: 11 points each, from a 1973 paper that made them up to show that summary numbers can hide the shape.
claims.source: Anscombe (1973), 'Graphs in Statistical Analysis', American Statistician 27(1): 17-21. Values typed from the published table (also widely reproduced); verify against the paper. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Anscombe (1973), 'Graphs in Statistical Analysis', The American Statistician 27(1): 17-21. All 44 x,y values in Demo.tsx match the published quartet as I know it (also the R datasets::anscombe table); not re-opened from the paper here.

claims.text: All four sets have mean x 9.0, mean y 7.5, correlation r = 0.82 (0.816) and the best-fit line y = 3.00 + 0.50x.
claims.source: stats() in Demo.tsx on the plotted points, node: slope 0.5001 / 0.5000 / 0.4997 / 0.4999; intercept 3.000 / 3.001 / 3.003 / 3.002; r 0.8164 / 0.8162 / 0.8163 / 0.8165; means 9.0 and 7.50. Readouts are computed per set; the question's r and the reveal's line come from set I. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): node: means 9 and 7.50; slopes 0.5001/0.5000/0.4997/0.4999; intercepts 3.000-3.002; r 0.8162-0.8165; also var x 11.0, var y 4.12-4.13 for the stage's 'same spread'.

claims.text: Set I is a loose cloud, set II a smooth curve, set III a tight line with one outlier, set IV ten points at x = 8 and one far to the right that alone sets the slope.
claims.source: A reading of the plots (stated as the stage notes); set IV: x values 8 x 10 and 19 (node). Not a statistical test. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Reading of the plots, labelled as such on the stage; set IV x = 8 (x10) and 19.

claims.text: Means, spread and correlation cannot tell these sets apart; always draw the data.
claims.source: Follows from c2 and c3: identical summaries, different pictures. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Follows from c2 and c3.

recall.question: Two datasets have the same mean, spread and correlation. What can you conclude about how they look?
options: Nothing: they can look very different, so plot them
recall.why: Summary numbers drop information. Anscombe's four sets share one fitted line yet are a cloud, a curve, an outlier and a single extreme point.
